Goodbye my holiday

By: Sophia Phirippides | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The fuel price is at a record high - how will it affect your December road trip

Unique Selling Point:
A satirical and light hearted consumer approach for our middle class viewers who are being taxed to death

Summary:
It’s the summer holidays, there is a brief respite from endless waves of the pandemic and you can bet on fatigued South African’s wanting to pack up their lives and head either to family homes in rural areas, up or down country and to the beach. But think again – many middle class families may not be able to afford to go anywhere, because unless they have been saving all year the latest petrol price increase may hobble their plans. The cost of filling up a tank with diesel is close to R6-00 more per litre than it was a year ago. Here is a small anecdotal example. We plan to show three routes out of Gauteng and what it will cost you

Further information:
JOHANNESBURG TO THE CAPE It will take 5 tanks of fuel at around R1300 per tank to fill up a Fortuner – that is what is needed to get from Johannesburg to the southern cape coast and back. Two tanks down, one tank there, and another two for the return journey will set you back about R6500. TOLLS FOOD ETC Now add a minimum of R500 for tolls both ways depending on your destination. You may also need tyres and a service before you go. Let’s leave the tyres and say just a small service of around R2000. So here we are at R9000 rand. Now imagine you have four people in the vehicle – that works out at around another R400 per journey – ( R100 pp minimum) if mom doesn’t make sandwiches, that adds another R800 rand to your journey. You are now sitting on a whopping R9800, and remember we are being very conservative. ACCOMODATION But the journey is long and you may wish to stop over for a night. If you are lucky you will find cheap digs for R300 per person per night. Add another R1200 each way and your journey to your destination and back alone has already cost you R12 200, and that is before you have paid for any accommodation and meals at your destination. Yikes! The AA have been highly critical of the latest petrol price increases that were delayed and then snuck through just minutes before polling closed on the 1st of November. Unleaded 95 in Gauteng is now 39.47% more expensive than it was 11 months ago and the coastal price is just over 40% more expensive. Diesel is 30% more expensive than it was at the beginning of the year, up by a remarkable R1.48 cents a litre. So basically R20:00 per litre as we head into the festive season. Happy Christmas all. To give an idea of what these increases are like OUTA has done a table of the petrol price over 10 years. From November 2011 to November 2021 it has increased by 81%. And all the levies combined have increased by 126%. In a Carte Blanche light but satirical piece we speak to OUTA and the AA and we take a few popular strip routes from Gauteng to Durban, to CT and to Limpopo and show exactly how much you will get stung if you want to escape to forget about life for a while, fill up your car and enjoy a coffee and a sandwich on your way out.

Press Release:


For months now many South Africans have been missing their relatives back home, or itching to have a break from work-at-home life. But the barrage of fuel hikes could confine them at home this December.

Script:


VO: As a tough year draws to a close, many South Africans are looking forward to a much-needed break.
Lyric: you know it’s time for a holiday...
LINK: if you're planning a road trip to your favourite holiday destination this December or simply going home to see your relatives across provinces, you may have to think twice with the fuel price skyrocketing your breakaway could just break the bank

Anuschka: Going to Mossel bay in December no, I tell you it's not going to happen. It's just too expensive.

VO: Anuschka Bannister and her family live in Heidelberg Gauteng. Mossel Bay in the Western Cape is their favoured destination, but on a teacher's salary and even though her husband holds down two jobs, this year it's unaffordable.

Anuschka: We might need to consider to come up with maybe to Ballito with somewhere closer.
Derek:: So what it means is a long road trip has now become a luxury.
Anuschka: that's true.
Derek: How much does it cost to fill up your Bakkie?
Anuschka: About R1500/ R1600

VO: Aside from having to rethink holiday plans, the Bannisters have daily fuel challenges.
Anuschka: We stay in Mid Vaal ,. And I work in Johannesburg and my husband works in the Vaal he drives to the Vaal every day so 140 kilometres per day for him as well.

VO: As a teacher, she’s able to catch a ride on the school bus with her children.

Derek: And if there wasn't the school bus, could you afford to travel to Bedfordview every school day?
Anuschka: Definitely not. I don't think I would have been able to, to pay the bills.

VO: With fuel prices breaking the R20 per litre barrier in Gauteng on the 1st of December, increases of 75 cents on petrol and around 74 cents on the unregulated price of diesel mean South Africans are in for a rough ride. Petrol alone has increased by almost R6 over the last year. Even so, Layton Beard, spokesperson for the Automobile Association of South Africa (AA), is optimistic about holiday travel this December.

Layton: I think given that we were in lockdown for most of last year, people will make plans to accommodate for these increases, even if it will hurt their pockets a bit, but certainly I think we’ll still see a lot of traffic on the roads.

VO: So how painful will the sting be this year? We took three popular routes from Johannesburg - to Cape Town, Durban and Tzaneen, and estimated the costs at the inland price of R20,29 per litre for 95 octane petrol, with a consumption of 8 litres per 100 kilometres and an additional 500 kilometres for day trips, plus national tolls.
Our first Route to Cape Town includes 4 tolls along the 1400 kilometre journey
Derek: After all the tension of tolls and the traffic you really need a holiday at the end of the journey I think.
VO: A round trip comes to a whopping total of R5 750 - about one and a half thousand rands more than last year.// Never mind the accommodation costs at your perfect getaway. According to Economist Sifiso Skenjana, those prices are up.

Sifiso: What we're seeing is that there's a lot of inflation from the cost of accommodation point of view that I think these providers are trying to make up for losses that they made when people weren't travelling.

VO: Next - a beach holiday in Durban, a mere 570 km away with 10 toll gates both ways, the travel alone comes to a hefty R 3 196 and that's if you didn't add a pitstop. //
BEAT// FOR A BIT OF IRONY

LINK: So I got myself a big burger and cafe mocha. Very larnie. Let's look at the costs - now the burger without chips was 85,90. Coffee was 41 bucks I remember when they used to cost about 10 but that was a long time ago... So we’re looking at just short of 127 rands, so a family of four you're looking at over 500 bucks, can you believe it?

VO: In South Africa, 84% of all goods are transported by road - that means that the cost of petrol and diesel transfers to the pricing of those goods.

Sifiso: We've seen oil prices now elevated, that the highest have been since October 2018. In fact, year on year oil prices are up 68%. Petrol prices tend to contribute about 25% of inflation levels in the country.

VO: At one of our refuels we met Gideon Lekobotja, an eco plastic furniture maker, with his fiance Sonto Vilakazi, they were hoping to see their family in Limpopo this December.

Gideon: According to the petrol rates, is not going to be easy for me to go home - is very difficult, because now the budget is low, especially under the COVID. We don't do much work.

VO: Our final route - to Tzaneen in Limpopo is 1320 kilometres, including day trips, with 3 toll gates each way, totals a staggering R2 385.

Sifiso: And then you need to factor in issues of wear and tear. You need to factor in what happens when you have a burst tire along the way, and then you're eating and all of those things, and these are the costs that are embedded in travel.

VO: We asked the AA to provide us with a total cost per kilometre including wear and tear on our Hyundai Creta, and it works out at R 5,22 per kilometre, so the real cost of our Tzaneen trip is more like R 7000. And it's not just holidaymakers that are affected.

Sifiso: We've got a society of people who are migrant workers. Our mine workers mostly come from Limpopo and the Eastern Cape. And so these are the people who need to go home at this time of the year as well

VO: So what do South Africans have to earn to afford long-distance travel? The Southern Africa Labour and Development Research Unit, Income Comparison Tool, puts it into perspective, says Skenjana.

Sifiso: the cost of living in South Africa is on average about 6400 per month. To then factor in two of those trips to and from home. Already, you are getting to about an earnings bracket of 10,000 Rand, in South Africa, people who are earning 10,000 Rand are actually in the top 10% of earners.
Derek: Is the term middle class a bit ambiguous these days?
Sifiso: What middle class? The middle class has ceased to exist in South Africa for quite a while now. If in South Africa, you earn 43,000 Rand a month you're in the top 1%

Derek: When did you last have a holiday?
Gideon: It's five years back. We can’t afford to go to the holiday, because even now it's difficult to manage to pay the employees and I left with nothing.
Derek: How does the fuel price affect your business?
Gideon: So it's very difficult for me to deal with clients. They want to cancel their orders because they said I'm so expensive.

VO: South Africa's bloated fuel price is dependent on a number of factors, the weakening rand and the increase in Brent Crude Oil, but if our fuel taxes were less we wouldn't be in such dire straits according to Wayne Duvenage CEO of the Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse, or OUTA.

Derek: Take us through all the extras.
Wayne: the fuel levy is one, it's a major one and then the road accident fund. The road accident fund is in a mess and that's gone up quite a lot in the last decade, about 173%, another 116% on the fuel Levy and then these other taxes, there’s 9/10 of them. so you add all of those up and they've also gone up 115% and some of them are avoidable. So you know a hundred and twenty-six percent increase in just the levy components over 10 years is excessive.

Layton: It's a tax that we feel hurts the poorest of the poor, because it gets added to every litre of fuel.

VO: Both OUTA and the AA are lobbying for no more increases to fuel levies next year, to allow South African motorists to catch their breath, particularly now that interest rates have also gone up.//
So how do families like the Bannisters adjust to their shrinking bottom line?

Anuschka: Honestly it boils down to less luxuries for us at the end of the day, sometimes even less trips to our families and friends

LINK: Putting fuel in the tank means so much more - it's the knock-on effect, getting to work, the kids to school and of course that long-awaited holiday but for millions of South Africans there won't be much choice.

Gideon There is nothing you can do, if you don't put fuel you can’t go to work. You don't have transport, you have nothing.

VO: For those who stretch their wallets for that moment in the sun, it may come with a few sacrifices along the way, although there is one sacrifice some South Africans - like me - can’t do without!

Derek: No road trip out of town is complete without that must-have packet of biltong.
Derek: How’re you doing? Afternoon -good to see you. That piece looks good right there. Now, this is the telling moment.
Hanri: Just gonna weigh it - R155
Derek: 155, What do you think of the cost of fuel these days?
Hanri: We can't go anymore where we want to go
Derek: So you’ll have to sell a lot more biltong?
Hanri: [laughs] yes!
Derek: Thanks very much Hanri
Hanri: Pleasure and enjoy and I hope to see you again.
Derek: Hopefully on the way back
Hanri: Alright, thank you, drive safely.

VO: And if we can't quite fill our tanks we can at least refuel and re-energise ourselves, ready to tackle a new year.

We can’t afford to go to the holiday, because even now it's difficult to manage to pay the employees and I left with nothing. Derek: How does the fuel price affect your business? Gideon: So it's very difficult for me to deal with clients. They want to cancel their orders because they said I'm so expensive. VO: South Africa's bloated fuel price is dependent on a number of factors, the weakening rand and the increase in Brent Crude Oil, but if our fuel taxes were less we wouldn't be in such dire straits according to Wayne Duvenage CEO of the Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse, or OUTA. Derek: Take us through all the extras. Wayne: the fuel levy is one, it's a major one and then the road accident fund. The road accident fund is in a mess and that's gone up quite a lot in the last decade, about 173%, another 116% on the fuel Levy and then these other taxes, there’s 9/10 of them. so you add all of those up and they've also gone up 115% and some of them are avoidable. So you know a hundred and twenty-six percent increase in just the levy components over 10 years is excessive. Layton: It's a tax that we feel hurts the poorest of the poor, because it gets added to every litre of fuel. VO: Both OUTA and the AA are lobbying for no more increases to fuel levies next year, to allow South African motorists to catch their breath, particularly now that interest rates have also gone up.// So how do families like the Bannisters adjust to their shrinking bottom line? Anuschka: Honestly it boils down to less luxuries for us at the end of the day, sometimes even less trips to our families and friends LINK: Putting fuel in the tank means so much more - it's the knock-on effect, getting to work, the kids to school and of course that long-awaited holiday but for millions of South Africans there won't be much choice. Gideon There is nothing you can do, if you don't put fuel you can’t go to work. You don't have transport, you have nothing. VO: For those who stretch their wallets for that moment in the sun, it may come with a few sacrifices along the way, although there is one sacrifice some South Africans - like me - can’t do without! Derek: No road trip out of town is complete without that must-have packet of biltong. Derek: How’re you doing? Afternoon -good to see you. That piece looks good right there. Now, this is the telling moment. Hanri: Just gonna weigh it - R155 Derek: 155, What do you think of the cost of fuel these days? Hanri: We can't go anymore where we want to go Derek: So you’ll have to sell a lot more biltong? Hanri: [laughs] yes! Derek: Thanks very much Hanri Hanri: Pleasure and enjoy and I hope to see you again. Derek: Hopefully on the way back Hanri: Alright, thank you, drive safely. VO: And if we can't quite fill our tanks we can at least refuel and re-energise ourselves, ready to tackle a new year.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The fuel price is at a record high - how will it affect your December road trip
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A satirical and light hearted consumer approach for our middle class viewers who are being taxed to death
metadata.Summary: It’s the summer holidays, there is a brief respite from endless waves of the pandemic and you can bet on fatigued South African’s wanting to pack up their lives and head either to family homes in rural areas, up or down country and to the beach. But think again – many middle class families may not be able to afford to go anywhere, because unless they have been saving all year the latest petrol price increase may hobble their plans. The cost of filling up a tank with diesel is close to R6-00 more per litre than it was a year ago. Here is a small anecdotal example. We plan to show three routes out of Gauteng and what it will cost you
metadata.Further information: JOHANNESBURG TO THE CAPE It will take 5 tanks of fuel at around R1300 per tank to fill up a Fortuner – that is what is needed to get from Johannesburg to the southern cape coast and back. Two tanks down, one tank there, and another two for the return journey will set you back about R6500. TOLLS FOOD ETC Now add a minimum of R500 for tolls both ways depending on your destination. You may also need tyres and a service before you go. Let’s leave the tyres and say just a small service of around R2000. So here we are at R9000 rand. Now imagine you have four people in the vehicle – that works out at around another R400 per journey – ( R100 pp minimum) if mom doesn’t make sandwiches, that adds another R800 rand to your journey. You are now sitting on a whopping R9800, and remember we are being very conservative. ACCOMODATION But the journey is long and you may wish to stop over for a night. If you are lucky you will find cheap digs for R300 per person per night. Add another R1200 each way and your journey to your destination and back alone has already cost you R12 200, and that is before you have paid for any accommodation and meals at your destination. Yikes! The AA have been highly critical of the latest petrol price increases that were delayed and then snuck through just minutes before polling closed on the 1st of November. Unleaded 95 in Gauteng is now 39.47% more expensive than it was 11 months ago and the coastal price is just over 40% more expensive. Diesel is 30% more expensive than it was at the beginning of the year, up by a remarkable R1.48 cents a litre. So basically R20:00 per litre as we head into the festive season. Happy Christmas all. To give an idea of what these increases are like OUTA has done a table of the petrol price over 10 years. From November 2011 to November 2021 it has increased by 81%. And all the levies combined have increased by 126%. In a Carte Blanche light but satirical piece we speak to OUTA and the AA and we take a few popular strip routes from Gauteng to Durban, to CT and to Limpopo and show exactly how much you will get stung if you want to escape to forget about life for a while, fill up your car and enjoy a coffee and a sandwich on your way out.
